panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT panel from a case report of proven chronic disseminated candidiasis, showing multiple hepatic nodules with marked rim enhancement, a classic hepatosplenic candidiasis imaging pattern. B: Contrast-enhanced ultrasound panel from the same patient with chronic disseminated candidiasis, showing multiple hypoechoic liver lesions. The vocabulary lacks a specific hepatic ultrasound finding, so the finding is proposed. C: Abdominal MRI panel from a case report of chronic disseminated candidiasis, showing multiple circular abnormal signal lesions in liver and spleen, consistent with hepatic microabscesses on MRI. D: 18F-FDG PET/CT panel from the same patient with chronic disseminated candidiasis, showing multiple hypermetabolic lesions in liver and spleen. No exact PET finding exists in the vocabulary, so the finding is proposed.

in_text_mentions: acid dehydrogenase of 185 U/L (140-280 U/L), aspartate aminotransferase of 16-20 U/L (8-33 U/L), alanine aminotransferase of 15 U/L (4-36 U/L), albumin of 4.0-4.1 g/dL (3.5-5.5 g/dL), and total bilirubin of 0.4-0.5 mg/dL (0.1-1.2 mg/dL). CT of the chest and abdomen showed atherosclerosis of the aorta but no dissection or stenosis. Enlargement of mediastinal, periportal, and retroperitoneal lymph nodes was noted (Figure 1).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). C: Fused PET/CT panel showing the FDG-avid hepatic and splenic lesions characteristic of chronic disseminated (hepatosplenic) candidiasis in this disease-focused article. in_text_mentions: The patient’s glucose level was estimated at 94 mg/dL. 18F-FDG PET/CT scan showed multiple foci of intense FDG uptake in the liver; the largest uptake was reported in segment VI and the spleen (Figure 1). No other pathological uptakes were discovered in the rest of the body, particularly lymphatic tissues. The subsequent abdominal CT scan confirmed the presence of multiple hypodense hepatic and splenic lesions, resembling microabscesses (Figure 2).

panels.figure_caption: Multiple visceral, intramuscular, and subcutaneous abscesses. Hypoechoic lesion without vascularity in the spleen (A). Hypoechoic and target‐shaped lesions in the periphery of hepatic parenchyma (B) Multiple thick‐walled cystic lesions containing some internal echogenic foci are seen in the subcutaneous area and within the medial muscular compartment of the right leg (C, D). Another intramuscular abscess with peripheral vascularity (E, F).
in_text_mentions: lower extremities with peripheral vascularity on Doppler ultrasound, suggesting of abscess formation. Multiple target‐shaped and hypoechoic lesions were also observed in the liver and spleen (Figure 1). Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the lower extremities was performed and showed numerous iso‐ to hypersignal on T1 and hypersignal on T2‐weighted oval lesions with hyposignal rim within different muscles of the lower extremities and also in subcutaneous tissue. The almost diffuse hyposignal intensity of the bone marrow of the bilateral tibia and fibula on the T1‐weighted sequence was also s

white arrows) (B). Axial T1 fat sat without contrast (C), axial T1 fat sat with contrast (D), and axial T2 fat sat images (E) show multiple iso to hypersignal T1 weighted, hypersignal T2‐weighted, oval‐shaped lesions in different muscles of legs, accompanied with ring enhancement. Coronal PD fat sat sequence (F) shows similar hypersignal lesions. Signal void foci on MRI (yellow star in A) were echogenic with faint acoustic shadow in the ultrasound exam (G), indicating calcification (a sign of response to treatment). Hypoechoic splenic lesions (Figure 1A) were calcified after the treatment (H).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Coronal abdominal CT of a real pediatric patient with captioned hepatomegaly and multiple splenic (blue arrows) and renal (yellow arrows) abscesses; article title and in-text interpretation explicitly identify these as splenic CDC in a child with ALL. [raw subtype: hepatosplenic candidiasis] B: Axial abdominal CT slice from the same pediatric patient showing enlarged liver/spleen with splenic abscesses marked by a blue arrow, attributed in the caption and article to chronic disseminated candidiasis. [raw subtype: hepatosplenic candidiasis]

panels.figure_caption: CT scan of abdomen Abdominal CT scan showing liver enlargement and multiple abscesses in the spleen (blue arrows) and kidneys (yellow arrows).
in_text_mentions: luconazole. Over the following days, the patient continued to have high-grade fever with tenderness and an increased number of subcutaneous lesions. On examination, enlarged cervical and axillary lymph nodes were also noted. A repeat CRP test was 117.43 mg/dl (normal < 0.8 mg/dl). Given the disseminated and metastatic nature of the infection, she was started on IV amphotericin-B. Full body imaging showed an enlarged liver and spleen, along with multiple abscesses in the spleen, kidneys, scalp, abdominal wall, and gluteus muscles (Figure 2). These findings indicated the presence of splenic CDC.
